## tables {#api-tables}

The data: writing rows into tables, and looking at what they hold. Tables are declared in `tables/*.yaml`; every table gets these endpoints.

### `POST /v1/tables/{table}/rows` {#op-ingestrows}

**Write rows into a table** · access: `ingest`

The body is the rows, in one of three formats, chosen by `Content-Type`: `application/json` (an array of row objects), `application/x-ndjson` (one row object per line) or `application/vnd.apache.arrow.stream` (an Arrow IPC stream, matched to columns by field name).

Values are checked against the table's column types and never coerced. A batch is all or nothing: one bad value rejects it with every problem listed by row and column, and nothing is written. On an upsert table a row whose key exists replaces the old row, and a row equal to the one stored is skipped: it counts as neither written nor replaced, and a batch of such rows changes nothing and is visible at once.

Rows become visible to queries at the next epoch (within `epoch_interval`); `?wait=visible` answers only once they are. An `Idempotency-Key` header makes retries safe: a key seen in the last 24 hours gets the first response again and writes nothing. A `503` means the server is busy; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | The table, by name. | `orders` |

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wait` | `visible`: answer once the rows are visible to queries. | `visible` |

Request: rows: JSON, NDJSON or Arrow IPC. The rows.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`IngestResponse`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingestresponse) | Written. |
| `400` | [`IngestError`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingesterror) | The body didn't decode, or a value doesn't fit its column. Nothing was written. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such table. |
| `409` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | A request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed, or the table was removed by a config change meanwhile. |
| `415` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | A `Content-Type` that isn't one of the three formats. |
| `503` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | Busy: the write queue is full. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds. |

### `DELETE /v1/tables/{table}/rows` {#op-deleterows}

**Delete rows from an upsert table, by key** · access: `ingest`

The body lists keys, in the same formats as writing: each row holds the table's primary key columns and nothing else. Keys that match no row are counted in `missing`, not treated as errors. Only upsert tables have keys, so only they can be deleted from this way.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | The table, by name. | `customers` |

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wait` | `visible`: answer once the deletes are visible to queries. | `visible` |

Request: rows: JSON, NDJSON or Arrow IPC. The keys of the rows to delete.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`IngestResponse`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingestresponse) | Deleted. |
| `400` | [`IngestError`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingesterror) | The body didn't decode, or the table isn't an upsert table. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such table. |
| `409` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | The table was removed by a config change meanwhile. |
| `503` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | Busy: retry after `Retry-After` seconds. |

### `PUT /v1/tables/{table}/rows` {#op-replacerows}

**Replace an upsert table's contents** · access: `ingest`

The body is the table's complete new contents, in the same formats as writing: its rows are written (a row whose key exists replaces the old one), and every row whose key isn't among them is deleted, in one batch that becomes visible at once. For keeping a dimension in step with a system of record that can only be read whole (an asset tree, a product catalogue): send all of it every time, and what disappeared there disappears here. Rows that are already as sent are skipped, so sending the same contents again changes nothing. `replaced` counts rows replaced and rows deleted. Only upsert tables have keys, so only they can be replaced.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | The table, by name. | `customers` |

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wait` | `visible`: answer once the new contents are visible to queries. | `visible` |

Request: rows: JSON, NDJSON or Arrow IPC. Every row the table should hold.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`IngestResponse`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingestresponse) | Replaced. |
| `400` | [`IngestError`](/reference/schemas#schema-ingesterror) | The body didn't decode, a value doesn't fit its column, or the table isn't an upsert table. Nothing was written. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such table. |
| `409` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | A request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed, or the table was removed by a config change meanwhile. |
| `415` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | A `Content-Type` that isn't one of the three formats. |
| `503` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | Busy: the write queue is full. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds. |

## queries {#api-queries}

Asking the model: metrics grouped by fields, under a selection. Names are the semantic layer's (`model.ossie.yaml`), not tables'.

### `POST /v1/query` {#op-query}

**Run a query** · access: `read`

Metrics grouped by dimensions, under a selection, from the newest snapshot: the engine dashboards use, without a subscription. Filters are one-directional: a metric is filtered by the fields its table reaches through relationships, and the rest don't apply to it.

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `csv` for the answer as CSV (a header of column names, then the rows), for spreadsheets and exports. JSON otherwise. | `json` |

Request: [`QueryRequest`](/reference/schemas#schema-queryrequest). What to compute.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`QueryResult`](/reference/schemas#schema-queryresult) or CSV | The answer. |
| `400` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | The query names something the model doesn't have, or asks for something the engine can't do. |

### `POST /v1/rows` {#op-rows}

**Read the newest rows** · access: `read`

The newest rows of a table that pass the filters, newest first (the order they arrived in): a log tail. A `contains` filter searches a string field for a text, ignoring the case of ASCII letters, and is fast on `encoding: plain` columns of the table itself. Filters are one-directional, as in a query: the fields the table reaches through relationships filter its rows.

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `csv` for the rows as CSV, JSON otherwise. | `json` |

Request: [`RowsRequest`](/reference/schemas#schema-rowsrequest). Which rows, and which of their fields.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`QueryResult`](/reference/schemas#schema-queryresult) or CSV | The rows, newest first, one column per field. |
| `400` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | A field the model doesn't have, or no table reaching all of them. |

### `GET /v1/ws` {#op-live}

**Live dashboards (WebSocket)** · access: `read`

Upgrades to a WebSocket speaking the live protocol: JSON messages tagged by `type` (`ClientMessage` in, `ServerMessage` out). A session holds a selection with back/forward history and shows one dashboard; the server sends one frame per epoch with whatever changed on it, and answers selection changes right away. Browsers can't set headers on a WebSocket, so the read token may also come as `?token=`.

| query parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | The read token, when one is configured. | `s3cret` |

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `101` | none | Switching to the WebSocket protocol. |

### `POST /v1/views` {#op-createview}

**Make a view** · access: `read`

A view is a dashboard that lives only in the server's memory: checked by the same rules as a dashboard file and shown live like one (`open_dashboard` with its id), but never written to the config, versioned or committed. For an answer an agent shows once; saving it as a dashboard is a config change like any other. The body is a dashboard file as JSON (the `dashboard` schema); a visual without `at` is placed for you. A view nobody opens for 24 hours is forgotten, and at most 1000 are kept.

Request: JSON. A dashboard file, as JSON.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ViewInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-viewinfo) | The view: its id, and what it shows. |
| `422` | [`ViewProblems`](/reference/schemas#schema-viewproblems) | The dashboard doesn't compile: its problems. |

### `GET /v1/views/{id}` {#op-getview}

**A view** · access: `read`

A view made with `POST /v1/views`: what it shows, and its dashboard file as YAML, ready to save under `dashboards/`.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | The view's id, as making it answered. | `~3f9c2a7d41b0e85c6d2f1a9b7e4c3d20` |

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ViewInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-viewinfo) | The view. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such view, or it was forgotten. |

### `GET /v1/model` {#op-getmodel}

**The semantic model** · access: `read`

Datasets and their fields, relationships, and metrics with their SQL, anchor table and the dashboards that show them: what the model browser shows.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ModelInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-modelinfo) | The model. |

### `POST /mcp` {#op-mcp}

**MCP for agents** · access: `read`

The Model Context Protocol over Streamable HTTP: JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, each answered with one JSON body. `tools/list` lists the tools (the MCP reference has each one) and `resources/list` the config files' JSON Schemas. Each tool is the HTTP endpoint it wraps, called with the caller's credentials, so tools that change the config need the admin token and ingest_rows the ingest token. apply_change applies what `agents.auto_apply` allows and proposes the rest.

Request: JSON. A JSON-RPC message, or a batch of them.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | JSON | The JSON-RPC reply (or replies). |
| `202` | none | A notification: nothing to reply. |

## config {#api-config}

Changing what the server runs while it runs: the config files, plans of what a change does, applying it, the versions so far and changes waiting for approval. Every change goes through the same pipeline, and is written back to the config directory.

### `GET /v1/config` {#op-getconfig}

**The config** · access: `admin`

Every config file of the current version, the version the server runs (behind while a change is rebuilt), and edits in the config directory that aren't applied.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ConfigState`](/reference/schemas#schema-configstate) | The config. |

### `POST /v1/config/plan` {#op-planconfig}

**What a change would do** · access: `admin`

Compiles the config with the change and compares it with the current one: every problem, located, and every change with its class (safe, rebuild, destructive). Changes nothing.

Request: [`ConfigChange`](/reference/schemas#schema-configchange). Files to set or remove, against a version.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`PlanInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-planinfo) | The plan (also when the config has errors: `valid` says). |
| `409` | [`ConfigError`](/reference/schemas#schema-configerror) | `base_version` isn't the current version. |

### `POST /v1/config/apply` {#op-applyconfig}

**Apply a change** · access: `admin`

Plans the change and applies it: safe changes are live at the next epoch, rebuilds when their background rebuild is done (the old version serves until then). A destructive change needs `approve`. With `propose` it waits in the approval queue instead. Applied changes are written back to the config directory, and committed when it is a git repository.

Request: [`ConfigChange`](/reference/schemas#schema-configchange). Files to set or remove, against a version.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ApplyResult`](/reference/schemas#schema-applyresult) | Applied, rebuilding, queued, or nothing to change. |
| `409` | [`ConfigError`](/reference/schemas#schema-configerror) | `base_version` isn't current, the change destroys data and isn't approved, or a rebuild is still running. |
| `422` | [`ConfigError`](/reference/schemas#schema-configerror) | The config doesn't compile with the change. |

### `GET /v1/config/versions` {#op-listconfigversions}

**Versions so far** · access: `admin`

Every applied version, newest first: who, when, from where, and what changed. Reverting is applying an old version's files.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | list of [`VersionInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-versioninfo) | The versions. |

### `GET /v1/config/versions/{version}` {#op-getconfigversion}

**One version's files** · access: `admin`

The files of an applied version, to compare or revert to.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | The version number. | `1` |

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ConfigVersion`](/reference/schemas#schema-configversion) | The version. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such version. |

### `GET /v1/changes` {#op-listchanges}

**Changes waiting for approval** · access: `admin`

Proposed changes, and edits in the config directory that aren't safe to apply on their own, with their plans.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | list of [`PendingChange`](/reference/schemas#schema-pendingchange) | The pending changes. |

### `POST /v1/changes/{id}/approve` {#op-approvechange}

**Approve a pending change** · access: `admin`

Applies it, destructive or not. It must still be against the current version.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | The pending change. | `1` |

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ApplyResult`](/reference/schemas#schema-applyresult) | Applied or rebuilding. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such pending change. |
| `409` | [`ConfigError`](/reference/schemas#schema-configerror) | It was made against an older version, or a rebuild is running. |

### `POST /v1/changes/{id}/reject` {#op-rejectchange}

**Reject a pending change** · access: `admin`

Drops it from the queue.

| path parameter | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | The pending change. | `1` |

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`PendingChange`](/reference/schemas#schema-pendingchange) | The change, now dropped. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No such pending change. |

## server {#api-server}

The process itself: probes for orchestrators, and what server this is.

### `GET /v1/status` {#op-getstatus}

**What the server is doing** · access: `read`

Epoch, memory per table and for caches, live sessions, and the write-ahead log and checkpoints when data is kept on disk.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`StatusInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-statusinfo) | The status. |

### `POST /v1/auth/embed` {#op-startembed}

**A token for embedded views** · access: `read`

A short-lived token that opens only the views named, over `/v1/ws` (as `?token=`) and nowhere else: what a view shown inside another app (an MCP App in Claude or ChatGPT) connects with, so the read token never leaves the server. It ends after an hour unused, or when the server stops.

Request: [`EmbedRequest`](/reference/schemas#schema-embedrequest). The views it may open.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`EmbedToken`](/reference/schemas#schema-embedtoken) | The token. |
| `404` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | One of the views isn't there. |

### `POST /v1/auth/session` {#op-startsession}

**Start a browser session** · access: `public`

Trades the token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for a session cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`), good for the levels the token is: the UI does this so tokens stay out of URLs and logs. Sessions end after 12 idle hours, on sign-out, or when the server stops.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`SessionInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-sessioninfo) | The session's levels; the cookie is set. |
| `400` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | No bearer token. |
| `401` | [`ApiError`](/reference/schemas#schema-apierror) | The token is good for nothing here. |

### `GET /v1/auth/session` {#op-getsession}

**What this request may do** · access: `public`

The levels open to this request: by its session cookie, its bearer token, or because they need no token.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`SessionInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-sessioninfo) | The levels. |

### `DELETE /v1/auth/session` {#op-endsession}

**Sign out** · access: `public`

Ends this browser's session and clears its cookie.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`SessionInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-sessioninfo) | Signed out: what's left open to everyone. |

### `GET /metrics` {#op-metrics}

**Prometheus metrics** · access: `read`

The server in the Prometheus text format: rows, memory and segments per table, ingest requests and rows, epoch publish and live refresh times, query times, sessions, the log and checkpoints, a running rebuild. At the root, where scrapers look.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | text | The metrics. |

### `GET /healthz` {#op-health}

**Liveness probe** · access: `public`

Answers `200` whenever the process is serving HTTP at all. It says nothing about whether the data is ready to query; that is `GET /readyz`.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ProbeStatus`](/reference/schemas#schema-probestatus) | The process is up. |

### `GET /readyz` {#op-ready}

**Readiness probe** · access: `public`

Answers `200` once the server can take traffic, and `503` while it is still starting. Later, starting includes applying the config and recovering data from the WAL, which is why this is separate from `GET /healthz`: a restart should not be killed for being slow to recover.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ProbeStatus`](/reference/schemas#schema-probestatus) | Ready. |
| `503` | [`ProbeStatus`](/reference/schemas#schema-probestatus) | Up, but not ready yet. |

### `GET /v1/info` {#op-getinfo}

**Which server this is** · access: `public`

The server's name, version and API version.

| status | body | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | [`ServerInfo`](/reference/schemas#schema-serverinfo) | The server's identity. |

Kinds: `server` (tidepool.yaml), `table` (tables/*.yaml), `model` (model.ossie.yaml), `dashboard` (dashboards/*.yaml), and the JSON inside TIDEPOOL extensions: `metric-extension`, `field-extension`, `dataset-extension`, `relationship-extension`, `model-extension`.

| path parameter | description | example |

| status | body | description |

| `200` | JSON | The schema. |
